the "},{"id":"p4s3","text":"page, and the agent's commands run in WebContainers:

- 🌍 **"},{"id":"p5s2","text":"The container is online too.** The page's CORS policy is preloaded into every Node process it starts"},{"id":"p5s3","text":", so `fetch` inside the container retries a refused host through the proxy on its own — `http://exam"},{"id":"p5s4","text":"ple.com` answers there now, and it did not before.

- 💾 **Or a whole PC.*"},{"id":"p5s6","text":"* Settings → Machine swaps the container for v86 and offers **128 machines** — the whole of v86's ca"},{"id":"p5s7","text":"talog, from a 512-byte bootsector game to Windows 2000, **127 of them booting with nothing to set up"},{"id":"p5s8","text":"** — emulated x86, on its own screen, with the tool set that machine actually has.
- 🧭 **Or a browse"},{"id":"p5s9","text":"r.** The third machine is real tabs of the real web, and the assistant drives them three ways: the p"},{"id":"p5s10","text":"age structure (a labelled tree with a handle on everything clickable), the pixels, or JavaScript in "},{"id":"p5s11","text":"the page itself.
